themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 5 this week, up 1900% from the 8-week baseline of 0.2 complaints per week, signaling a potential surge in unlicensed or non-compliant retail operations in Mott Haven/Melrose that warrants investigation into enforcement gaps.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 average weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.97)
Represents 1900% increase from baseline, highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Pattern suggests recent acceleration in unauthorized retail operations or community awareness/reporting of existing illicit retailers
reporting_angles: Investigate whether unlicensed cannabis retailers have proliferated in the district; map locations and interview residents about access, youth sales concerns
Interview NYPD/local enforcement about why complaints spiked and what resources are allocated to enforcement; examine any gaps between state licensing authority and local enforcement

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Spikes This Week
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 4 this week, up 540% from the 8-week baseline of 0.6 per week, representing a sudden and significant change that could indicate new activity patterns, events, or lack of enforcement.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints filed this week vs. 0.6 average weekly baseline (z-score: 3.4)
Represents 540% spike—largest non-cannabis anomaly in recency-weighted analysis
Timing suggests recent change in park conditions, permitted events, or enforcement presence
reporting_angles: Identify which park(s) generated complaints and what activity triggered them; interview Parks Dept about event permits, maintenance, or enforcement
Canvass park users and nearby residents to understand if noise is from new uses (e.g., outdoor events, encampments, informal gatherings) or reduced enforcement

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Stay Elevated
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints hit 12 two weeks ago, representing a 465% spike from the 8-week baseline of 2.1 per week; while the spike occurred 2 weeks ago, it remains the second-highest statistical anomaly and suggests a sustained homelessness surge warranting investigation.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 average weekly baseline (z-score: 5.03)
Represents 465% increase and aligns with repeated community board budget requests for homeless services expansion
No follow-up data on whether encampments have been addressed or remain in place
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations from 311 data; interview residents about safety concerns, duration of encampments, and available resources; assess whether DHS outreach teams are present
Investigate why the district repeatedly requests expanded homelessness services in CB budgets (unfunded gaps); interview DHS about capacity and barriers to engagement in this district

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Complaints Up 700%
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints hit 3 two weeks ago, up 700% from the 8-week baseline of 0.4 per week; given the district's aging housing stock and concurrent brush with DOB building permits surge (421 filings including 289 alterations), this spike warrants investigation into renovation practices and lead disclosure compliance.
evidence: 3 lead complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 average weekly baseline (z-score: 5.42)
Represents 700% spike coinciding with 289 alteration permits filed in last 90 days—potential indicator of unsafe renovation practices in pre-1978 housing
Community board repeatedly requests additional building inspectors, suggesting existing inspection capacity is insufficient
reporting_angles: Cross-check lead complaints with DOB alteration permits in same addresses/timeframe; investigate whether renovations triggered lead hazards and whether contractors complied with disclosure/remediation rules
Interview residents and housing advocates about lead awareness; examine DOB enforcement actions and inspector capacity in the district relative to complaint volume

themes_detail.label: Sanitation & Missed Collections Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed garbage collection complaints jumped 522% to 7 last week (vs. 1.1 baseline), while sanitation worker complaints spiked 1100% to 3 three weeks ago; these concurrent spikes suggest systemic sanitation service failures warranting investigation into staffing, routes, or operational changes.
evidence: Missed collection complaints: 7 last week vs. 1.1 average weekly baseline (z-score: 3.33, up 522%)
Sanitation worker/vehicle complaints: 3 three weeks ago vs. 0.2 average weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35, up 1100%)
Convergence of two related service failures suggests operational or staffing issue rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine if there were staffing shortages, route changes, or equipment failures during the affected weeks; request collection completion data by district
Interview residents about uncollected garbage accumulation and how long it persists; assess public health and rodent/pest implications
